mainTopic: Testing רב הונא's rule that a seller who mixes in more than a quarter-קב of טינופת per סאה loses all of it, using sources about כלאים, deposits, interest documents and extra land.
overview: The גמרא keeps testing רב הונא's rule: if a seller mixes more than a quarter-קב of dirt (טינופת) into each סאה of produce, the buyer takes off all the dirt, not just the extra. First it asks how רבי יוסי can demand that all foreign seeds be picked out in the כלאים משנה. The answer is that his reason is special: leaving some would look like keeping כלאים on purpose. Next it brings the משנה of two people who deposited money with one person, along with רבי יוסי's view there. Then it brings the ברייתא about a loan document with interest, with both רבי מאיר's view and the חכמים' view. Each time the גמרא answers with הכי השתא: the cases are not alike, because with the seller we never know how much dirt, if any, he mixed in on purpose. Finally it brings רבין בר רב נחמן's teaching that a buyer who must return extra land returns all of it. The גמרא starts to reject that comparison, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the end of the משנה: רבי יוסי says pick it all out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the last line of the כלאים משנה, where רבי יוסי says one must remove all the foreign seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part of the משנה: רבי יוסי says: he must pick out all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It quotes רבי יוסי's opinion from the end of the משנה it just discussed, so it can use it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained the first part of the משנה (just reduce the foreign seeds) by saying a quarter in כלאים is like exactly a quarter of dirt, which carries no penalty. רבי יוסי's harsher ruling at the end of the משנה now threatens that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (of the משנה or ברייתא)
He must pick out (all the foreign seeds)
The תנא who gives the stricter view in this משנה

phrases.english: Say the last part of the משנה:
Rabbi Yosei says: he must pick it all out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the earlier answer that a quarter in כלאים is like exactly a quarter of טינופת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer comparing a quarter of foreign seeds to exactly a quarter of dirt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי demands full removal, which fits better if the case is like more than a quarter, where a penalty applies.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוסי demand full removal if it is only a quarter?
steps.stepSummary: If a quarter in כלאים is like more than a quarter of dirt, the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי simply argue about penalizing. But if it is like exactly a quarter, רבי יוסי's ruling makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say it is like more than a quarter of dirt. Then this is their argument: the תנא קמא holds we do not penalize the permitted part because of the forbidden part, and רבי יוסי holds we do penalize. But if you say it is like exactly a quarter, why must he pick out all of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge. רבי יוסי's ruling fits only if the case is like more than a quarter of dirt, and that undoes the earlier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is like more than a quarter, the argument is a clean dispute about penalties (קנס). The תנא קמא only makes you remove the excess, and רבי יוסי makes you remove everything, just like רב הונא. But if it is like exactly a quarter, which is fully allowed, there is nothing to penalize, so רבי יוסי's demand seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
Dirt or waste mixed into produce
The permitted part because of the forbidden part
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two comparisons. 'Like more than a quarter' means a penalty is possible. 'Like exactly a quarter' means it is allowed, with nothing to penalize.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that it is like more than a quarter of dirt,
phrases.notes: The quarter of other seeds in the כלאים case is being compared to רב הונא's dirt case.

phrases.english: then this is what they argue about:
The first תנא holds:
we do not penalize the permitted part because of the forbidden part,
and Rabbi Yosei holds: we do penalize.
But if you say it is like exactly a quarter,
why must he pick out all of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the quoted line of רבי יוסי is a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a quarter in כלאים is like exactly a quarter of טינופת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exactly a quarter is allowed, so there is no reason to require removing everything. רבי יוסי's ruling only makes sense as a penalty for going over the limit.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's special reason: it looks like keeping כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's ruling is not a penalty. Leaving some foreign seeds after cleaning would look like he wants to keep כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, this is רבי יוסי's reason: because it looks as if he is keeping כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי's reason is special to כלאים and has nothing to do with penalties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person starts cleaning the seeds, purposely leaving some of the other kind looks like he wants כלאים in his field. So רבי יוסי's ruling tells us nothing about penalizing, and the comparison to exactly a quarter still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case, here כלאים)
Keeping mixed kinds of plants on purpose

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's ruling in כלאים is about how it looks, not about penalizing, so it does not prove anything about רב הונא's rule.

phrases.english: There, this is Rabbi Yosei's reason:
because it looks as if he is keeping mixed kinds.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for רבי יוסי, separate from the question of penalties.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי requires full removal as a penalty, so the case must be like more than a quarter.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי requires full removal because leaving some looks like keeping כלאים, even if the amount is exactly a quarter.

steps.title: New challenge: two depositors who both claim two hundred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about two people who deposited money with one person. There, the חכמים do not penalize the liar by holding back everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: two people deposited money with one person, one a מנה (100) and the other two hundred. This one says 'the two hundred is mine,' and that one says 'the two hundred is mine.' He gives this one a מנה and that one a מנה, and the rest stays put away until אליהו comes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב הונא by quoting a משנה. The point being drawn from it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One depositor is clearly lying, yet each still gets the hundred that is certainly his. Only the disputed hundred is held back. That looks like no penalty, which goes against רב הונא's idea of penalizing the seller by taking away everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a new source is being brought)
A coin worth one hundred זוז
Until אליהו comes (until the truth can be known)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two people who deposited money with one person,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא מציעא (37a).

phrases.english: this one a hundred and that one two hundred;
this one says: 'The two hundred is mine,'
and that one says: 'The two hundred is mine' –
he gives this one a hundred and that one a hundred,
and the rest will be put away
until Elijah comes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כלאים challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new source against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that the seller is penalized and loses everything when he goes over the limit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the deposit case, the liar is not penalized by having all the money held back, so it seems the חכמים do not penalize the permitted part because of the forbidden part.

steps.title: The deposits case is different: each person surely owns one hundred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the challenge from the deposits משנה. There, each person surely owns one hundred, so the חכמים cannot take that away. Here, maybe the seller mixed in all the dirt on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison?! There, one hundred surely belongs to this person and one hundred surely belongs to that person. Here, who can say the seller did not mix in all of it on purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4 by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the deposits case, holding back everything would take away one hundred that surely belongs to each person, so there the חכמים do not penalize. In the dirt case, we have no proof that any of the dirt got in honestly. So taking off all of it is not taking away something that is surely the seller's.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a real comparison?! (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
To this person (literally, to the master)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the deposits case has no cheat. It is saying each side surely owns one hundred, and that sure ownership cannot be taken away.

phrases.english: Is that a real comparison?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, וַדַּאי מָנֶה לְמָר וּמָנֶה לְמָר;
phrases.english: There, surely one hundred belongs to this one and one hundred to that one;
Here, who can say
that he did not mix in all of it on purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought in Step 4 by distinguishing the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the חכמים do not penalize in the deposits case, they should not penalize the seller either.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the deposits case each side surely owns one hundred, so it cannot be taken away. The seller may have mixed in all the dirt on purpose, so removing all of it is allowed.

steps.title: A proof from רבי יוסי: hold everything until אליהו comes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to support the penalty from the end of the deposits משנה. There, רבי יוסי says to hold back all the money so the cheat loses out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from the end of that משנה: רבי יוסי said, if so, what did the cheat lose? Rather, all the money should be put away until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the penalty from רבי יוסי's opinion in the same deposits משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, if each person gets back one hundred, the cheat loses nothing by lying. So רבי יוסי holds back everything, even money that surely belongs to each of them. That looks like a penalty on a cheat, which fits רב הונא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (an opening for a proof)
The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
Until אליהו comes (held back with no end date)

phrases.english: Come and hear from the end part:
Rabbi Yosei said:
If so, what did the cheat lose?
Rather, everything should be put away
until אליהו comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is answered, the גמרא now uses the same משנה to support the penalty.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים penalize a cheat even by holding back money that is surely his, which supports רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי in the end part of the deposits משנה.

steps.title: No proof: there a cheat surely exists, here maybe not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the deposits case someone is surely lying. With the seller, maybe the dirt got in by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison?! There, there is surely a cheat. Here, who can say he mixed anything in on purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from רבי יוסי by showing a difference between the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי penalizes only because one of the two depositors is surely lying. With the produce, the dirt might have gotten mixed in without the seller meaning to. So רבי יוסי's penalty does not show that we would penalize the seller.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 5 said the seller might have mixed in all the dirt on purpose. Step 7 says he might not have mixed in any on purpose. Both are true: we do not know, and each answer uses a different side of that doubt.

phrases.english: Is that a real comparison?!
There, there is surely a cheat,
here, who can say that he mixed it in on purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the seller is surely a cheat. Unlike the deposits case, the dirt may have gotten in by accident.

steps.title: A new proof: רבי מאיר penalizes a loan document with interest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof for penalizing. רבי מאיר says a lender whose loan document includes interest cannot collect anything, not even the loan itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a loan document has interest written in it, we penalize the lender. He collects neither the loan amount nor the interest. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to support the idea of a penalty, the way רב הונא ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the interest is forbidden, yet רבי מאיר takes away even the loan amount, which is fully the lender's. That shows the חכמים penalize someone who did wrong by taking more than the forbidden part, just like taking off all the dirt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear case where the חכמים take away money that truly belongs to someone because he acted wrongly. That is exactly the kind of penalty רב הונא's ruling needs.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A loan document that has interest in it:
we penalize him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the lender, the one who wrote the interest into the document.

phrases.english: and he does not collect the loan amount
nor the interest;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי יוסי was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים penalize a wrongdoer by taking away even what is truly his, which supports רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי מאיר's ruling about a loan document that includes interest.

steps.title: The interest case is different because the lender clearly sinned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי מאיר. The lender sinned the moment he wrote interest into the document. The seller may never have mixed in dirt on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the lender put interest on the borrower right when the document was written. Here, who says the seller mixed anything in at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 8. It says the loan case and the dirt case are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the loan case, the sin is certain, because the interest is written right there in the document. That is why רבי מאיר can fine the lender. With the seller, the dirt may have gotten in by accident, so there may be nothing to punish.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
From the time of writing the document
Literally 'an assessment'; here, placing interest on the borrower

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, from the time of the writing
he placed interest on him,
here, who can say
that he mixed anything in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison between the loan document and the seller, not רבי מאיר's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lender surely sinned when he wrote the document. The seller may not have sinned at all.

steps.title: A challenge from the חכמים who let the lender collect the loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the end of the same ברייתא. The חכמים say the lender collects the loan itself, just not the interest. That suggests no penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the end of that teaching: The חכמים say he collects the loan amount, but he does not collect the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the second half of the ברייתא to challenge the idea of penalizing the seller. The חכמים do not fine the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים take away only the forbidden part, the interest, and let the lender keep the allowed part. Following that pattern, the seller should only lose the dirt beyond the allowed amount, not all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a teaching
The principal, the original loan amount

phrases.english: Come and hear from the end of the teaching:
But the Sages say:
He collects the principal,
but he does not collect the interest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the other half of the ברייתא from step 8, this time against the penalty
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the seller is penalized by losing all the dirt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים take away only the forbidden interest and do not fine the lender, so the seller should also lose only the extra dirt.

steps.title: The loan amount is surely allowed, but the dirt may all be the seller's fault
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the loan amount is certainly permitted, so it cannot be taken away. With the seller, maybe all the dirt was mixed in on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the loan amount is certainly permitted. Here, who says he did not mix in all of the dirt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge from the חכמים. It shows why their ruling does not apply to the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original loan is completely allowed money, so the חכמים leave it alone. With the dirt, we cannot know that any of it is innocent. Maybe the seller added all of it, so losing all of it is fair.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, the principal certainly
is permitted,
here, who can say
that he did not mix in all of it?

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the חכמים take away only the forbidden part, the seller should only lose the extra dirt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loan amount is surely permitted, so it is not touched. None of the dirt is surely innocent, so the seller can lose all of it.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 9 said 'maybe he mixed in nothing,' and this step says 'maybe he mixed in everything.' Each answer only has to show that the source does not fit our case, so the two do not contradict each other.

steps.title: Proof from the field that was bigger than promised
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב נחמן teaches that if a buyer must return extra land, he returns all of the extra, not just the part beyond the allowed amount. The same should be true for the dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבין בר רב נחמן taught: He does not return only the part beyond the limit. He returns all of the extra quarters. So when someone has to give back, he gives back everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof to support penalizing the seller. It uses a ruling about a land sale where the field was bigger than stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small difference in a field's size is overlooked. But once the extra land goes past that limit, the buyer must return all of it, even the small part that would normally be overlooked. The גמרא concludes that once the limit is crossed, everything gets returned, just like the seller with too much dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who taught this ברייתא
The extra, the part beyond the limit

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would give רב הונא a general rule: once a sale goes past the allowed margin, the margin is lost too and everything must be returned. The next step rejects the comparison with הכי השתא.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Ravin bar Rav Naḥman teaches:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַמּוֹתָר בִּלְבַד הוּא מַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: He does not return only the extra,
rather he returns to him
every one of the quarters.
Apparently, where he needs to return,
he returns all of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the loan ברייתא were pushed away, a new source is brought for the penalty
steps.raayaObject: That the seller must take back all the dirt, not just the part beyond the allowed amount
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבין בר רב נחמן: once the extra land passes the limit, the buyer returns all the extra quarters

steps.title: The land case is not like the dirt case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבין בר רב נחמן's teaching about extra land with the exclamation הכי השתא, meaning the cases are not comparable.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare these two cases?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just brought from the extra land case and says the two cases are not alike. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain what makes them different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, the land rule was used to argue that the seller should lose all the extra dirt, not just the part beyond what is allowed. Here the גמרא says that comparison does not hold. The reason is given in the lines that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so now?!" An exclamation the גמרא uses to reject a comparison as not fitting.

steps.confusionAlert: הכי השתא is not a question asking for information. It is a sharp rejection that means "you cannot compare these!" The explanation comes next.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
phrases.notes: Literally "Is it like this now?!" It is rejecting the comparison to the extra land case from the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12 from רבין בר רב נחמן's land teaching.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the extra land case and the dirt-in-produce case. It does not reject רבין בר רב נחמן's land rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are claimed to be different. The specific difference is spelled out in the lines that follow.
